title: Onprem release telemetry and verify-hooks playbook (draft)
body:
Purpose:
This is a working draft focused on adding lightweight, reproducible verification hooks and release telemetry into our GitOps/Argo-based pipelines for private (VPC / on-prem) deployments. The goal is to make each rollout observable and automatically verifiable by short-lived cluster jobs so that the CI system (and Redwood Console) can gate promotions and surface actionable telemetry quickly.

Scope & assumptions:
- Applies to Dedicated & Private deployments managed via ArgoCD-style GitOps and Helm-based manifests.
- Assumes images are signed (cosign) and attested where required upstream of promotion.
- Assumes Terraform modules handle cluster bootstrap; this doc does not replace those modules but suggests hooks to wire into them.
- Not a full release policy spec — this is focused on telemetry and verification primitives to be embedded in pipelines.

High-level flow (summary):
1) Developer/automation pushes manifest changes to git (kustomize/helm tweaks, new image tag)
2) CI runs preflight static checks (helm lint, manifest schema, image signature presence check)
3) Argo sees new commit -> sync starts against target cluster(s)
4) Immediately after sync: a VerifyHook job (K8s Job) is created by a small controller (or Argo Rollouts hook) to run platform smoke tests and emit structured telemetry (JSON) to a telemetry endpoint (push to console/observability)
5) VerifyHook returns pass/fail; results are attached as an annotation on the release manifest and posted to CI via webhook
6) Rollout policy (canary / promoted) consumes the result; promotion proceeds only on pass or after configurable fallback timer

VerifyHook design (requirements):
- Lightweight and idempotent; runs in-cluster as a Job or Pod that terminates quickly (30s-5m)
- Runs a small set of probes: readiness checks, simple inference or health endpoint, basic DB ping (if applicable)
- Emits structured result: {status, metrics, checks:[{name, status, latency, details}]} (we will stringify for annotations)
- Uploads artifacts where relevant (small logs, trace ids) to a secure S3 endpoint or pushes to internal telemetry ingest with proper auth
- Verifies image provenance (cosign) as part of the job if not already enforced upstream
- Timeouts and retry semantics: 2 retries, exponential backoff, overall timeout configurable per team

Example VerifyHook checks (templated):
- readiness-http: GET /health -> 200 within 1s
- smoke-infer: POST /v1/generate with short prompt -> non-empty tokens and <200ms median latency
- kv-store-ping: connect to customer-provided Redis endpoint with test key (if present)
- config-check: verify secret exists and configmap contains expected keys

Embedding verify hooks in GitOps: options
- Option A: Operator-based: a small k8s controller (verify-hook-controller) watches ArgoCD Application sync events and creates Jobs, posts results back to Application as annotation + emits to telemetry. Pros: centralized, can coordinate multi-app checks. Cons: extra controller running in control plane.
- Option B: Argo Rollouts native hooks: use Rollout hooks to run Jobs during canary/promotion. Pros: native lifecycle ties, no extra controller. Cons: more coupling to Rollout API and RBAC boundaries.
- Option C: CI-driven post-sync verifier: CI (GitHub Actions) waits for Argo sync to complete and then triggers a remote verify job via k8s exec/remote-job API. Pros: CI-centric visibility. Cons: more latency, requires K8s credentials in CI.

Recommended pattern: start with Operator-based approach for consistency across Dedicated and private clusters. Build a small verify-hook-controller that:
- consumes a VerifyHook CRD attached to app manifests (simple annotation also acceptable)
- creates ephemeral Jobs, collects results, emits telemetry, and writes status back to Git (commit or comment) or posts to CI via webhook

Telemetry contract (minimal):
- Each VerifyHook submission must include: release_id, repo@sha, image_tag, cluster_id, app_name, timestamp, result.status (pass/fail/soft-fail), checks[].
- Result is pushed to telemetry endpoint over mTLS with client cert rotated by KMS (or to internal ingest through the private control plane in Private deployments).
- We should include an open schema and quick parser in the Console to show per-release verification tiles and link to logs/traces.

Preflight static checks (CI):
- helm lint / yamllint / kubeval
- image signature existence: quick cosign verify - this only validates presence of signature blob matching tag (not full policy)
- terraform plan: run module-level plan in a sandbox (for infra changes)
- manifest diff: ensure no binding of cluster-admin roles without explicit approval

Promotion & canaries
- Canary window should be linked to verify-hook results. Example policy: run verify-hook for initial canary (5% traffic) -> if pass, auto-promote to 25% -> run verify-hook again -> on pass promote to 100% otherwise rollback to previous image.
- If verify-hook returns soft-fail (e.g., flakey latency), attach a mitigation ticket automatically and optionally move to manual approval queue.

Rollbacks and safe-failures
- Automated rollback path: annotate Argo App with previous-image tag and let Argo revert. Verify-hook-controller should watch for rollbacks and run a post-rollback verification.
- If operator/controller fails to run (controller down), Argo should emit an event; we should have an alert in SRE for control-plane health.
- Fallback: if verification system is unreachable, honor a per-app policy: block promotion OR allow a time-limited bypass with audit log.

Image signing and provenance notes:
- Enforce cosign attestations for private clusters: require at least one build attest and one SBOM artifact linked to tag. VerifyHook should re-check presence and optionally validate attestation subject.
- Keep a compact image provenance record in a read-only S3 in the cluster namespace for quick lookups by support.

Terraform module integration points:
- terraform module outputs should include cluster_id, argo_app_namespace, cluster_kubeconfig_secret_name so CI or operator can find the app endpoints to call back to.
- Provide a module boolean enable_verify_hooks = true that wires default service account + RBAC for verify-hook-controller jobs.
- When creating airgapped bundles, the module should produce an artifact manifest listing images to be mirrored and their cosign signature URIs.

Operational checklist for adopting VerifyHooks (quick steps):
- [ ] Add cosign signing step to build pipelines and push attestation metadata to the registry (or artifact bucket)
- [ ] Add helm chart template for VerifyHook CRD or annotation (example included below)
- [ ] Deploy verify-hook-controller into control plane namespace with RBAC restricted to App namespaces
- [ ] Add CI preflight job to check for signature presence before PR merge
- [ ] Configure Console telemetry ingestion and dashboards for verify results
- [ ] Run a canary with intentional failure to validate rollback signals and ticket creation

Example annotation snippet to attach to k8s manifest (helm values):
annotations:
  redwood.dev/verify-hook: "true"
  redwood.dev/verify-hook-config: "smoke-infer,readiness-http,kv-store-ping"

Lightweight verify-job template (pseudo):
- image: redwood/verify-hook-runner:v0.2
- env: RELEASE_ID, REPO_SHA, IMAGE_TAG, TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT
- commands: run-checks --checks="$REDWOOD_CHECKS" --emit-json=/tmp/result.json && curl --cert /certs/client.pem -X POST $TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT -d @/tmp/result.json

Logging and observability:
- short logs should be preserved as a k8s job log and pushed to telemetry. For privacy, strip customer data before pushing outside the VPC for private clusters.
- include a trace id emitted by VerifyHook and pick up in the console with links to traces if available.

Outstanding questions / TODOs:
- How tightly do we want to couple verify hooks with RBAC? Does each team get a SA per namespace?
- Can we reuse Argo Rollouts webhooks entirely instead of operator for simpler installations? Need pilot with 2 customers.
- Decide on soft-fail semantics and how Console should display them (warning vs fail).
- Define retention policy for verify-run artifacts in private deployments (default 30 days).

Appendix: quick CI cosign verify example (for reference):
- cosign verify --key $KEY -a attestation=build ${REGISTRY}/${IMAGE}:${TAG} || exit 1

Notes to self / meeting action items:
- Sync w/ SRE about controller placement and alerting (Liam)
- Spike a minimal verify-hook-controller prototype and demo in staging (Sofia)
- Draft telemetry schema and console tile design (Ethan)

This doc is intentionally pragmatic — aim to ship a simple operator + CI preflight in Q1 and iterate. Keep this draft as the engineering playbook; later we will formalize an RFC for rollout policies and a customer-facing integration guide.
